newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen steel workers return to work.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen steel workers return to work.

text.p: Thousands of steel workers at Thyssen Stahl AG who downed tools this week to protest a hostile takeover attempt by rival Krupp returned to work on a limited basis, the works council said on Wednesday.

Following an announcement that Krupp and Thyssen were to begin talks aimed at forming a joint steel company, possibly averting a takeover by Krupp, the works council said they would await the outcome of the talks.

Thyssen Stahl works council head Dieter Kroll told a meeting of Thyssen Stahl workers in Duisburg they should go back to work, but he warned managers they were ready at any time to down their tools in protest again.
Workers would return to work this afternoon but it would take a couple of shifts to get back to full production probably on Thursday afternoon, Kroll said.
"We are ready to mobilise (stop work again) at any moment" Kroll told a gathering of workers after the meeting.
Kroll said there would still be a workers' meeting as planned on Friday held together with the Krupp workers.
"We need the facts before us before we can decide on our position," Kroll said. "The problems won't just be wiped off the table. We are watching this process critically."
Krupp and Thyssen have said they plan eight days of meetings to develop a common plan to create a jointly-owned steel company.
Should those talks fail, the two companies would return to the starting blocks and Krupp would probably renew its bid to Thyssen shareholders. -- Bonn Newsroom, 49 228 26097 150
